lastCompletedGameRecap.recapHeadline: Rams win their 4th straight game, overcoming a slow start to crush the Cardinals 34-6
lastCompletedGameRecap.recapLeadExcerpt: GLENDALE, Ariz.  -- — Beaux Limmer was snapping the ball, Xavier Smith and Davis Allen were catching it and Kamren Kinchens came up with a key interception.  These were not the star-studded Los Angeles Rams that entered the season with Super Bowl aspirations.  But the Rams continued to show their depth and resourcefulness Sunday in a 34-6 road victory over the Arizona Cardinals , picking up their fourth straight win heading into a much-needed bye week. ” Beck's debut starts with promise, ends poorly It was a mixed debut for Cardinals’ rookie quarterback Carson Beck , who made some nice throws early and completed 11 of 18 passes for 108 yards, but also threw two interceptions and faded toward the end of the game.  Jacoby Brissett was traded to the Baltimore Ravens on Nov.
lastCompletedGameRecap.inGameInjuryNotes: Injuries Rams: Centers Coleman Shelton (hamstring) and Dylan McMahon (knee) both left the game in the first half and didn't return. Limmer moved to center with both of them out. Cardinals: DL Jordan Burch (knee) left the game in the first quarter and didn't return.
lastCompletedGameRecap.upNextNotes: Up next Rams: Enter their bye week with the next game at home on Nov. 25 against Green Bay. Cardinals: At Kansas City next Sunday.

upcomingMatchup.kickoffDisplay: Wed, Nov 25, 5:00 PM PST • NFL TV

injuryReport.name: Micah Parsons
factors: Season-ending Injured Reserve — ineligible to return this season
injuryReport.beatComment: Parsons remains listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against the Rams, but he's fully expected to play in Week 12 in what will mark his 2026 debut. The five-time Pro Bowler will be making his first appearance since tearing the ACL and meniscus in his left knee Dec. 14, 2025 and requiring season-ending surgery. Parsons has worked exclusively as a limited participant in practice since being designated for return from the PUP list Nov. 4, so the Packers could monitor his snaps closely in his first game action in more than 11 months.

injuryReport.name: Luke Musgrave
factors: Officially ruled Out on weekly game status report
injuryReport.beatComment: LaFleur acknowledged that Musgrove is still in the process of rehabbing the neck injury he sustained during OTAs in June, and the Packers haven't yet prepared for the tight end to resume practicing. Barring dramatic progress in his recovery over the next month, Musgrave looks like he'll be sidelined for the final season of his rookie deal before hitting free agency in the spring.

injuryReport.name: Josh Jacobs
factors: Thursday Limited Participation (LP); player toughness prior = 76%
Beat consensus: unlikely / not expected to suit up
injuryReport.beatComment: Coming off a bye week, Jacobs went down as a limited participant in all three of the team's Week 12 practice sessions. While the Packers aren't closing the door on Jacobs suiting up Wednesday, head coach Matt LaFleur previously noted Sunday and Monday that the running back was still viewed as unlikely to play against the Rams. Before making a decision on Jacobs' status prior to Wednesday's 8 p.m. ET kickoff, the Packers could put him through a pregame workout to gauge if his surgically repaired right ring finger presents any issues with gripping or securing the football. If Jacobs is forced to miss a second consecutive game, Kaleb Johnson and MarShawn Lloyd would be in line to lead the Green Bay rushing attack for another week.

injuryReport.name: Zaire Franklin
factors: Consecutive Wed/Thu Limited (LP -> LP) following 4-game absence
injuryReport.beatComment: Franklin was limited in all three practices leading up to Wednesday night's showdown against the Rams. The questionable tag is positive news for the 30-year-old linebacker, as he's missed the past four games due to a shin injury.

injuryReport.name: Skyy Moore
factors: Thursday Limited Participation (LP); player toughness prior = 76%
injuryReport.beatComment: Moore was limited in all three practices ahead of Week 12 after re-injuring his ankle in Week 10 against the Vikings. The 26-year-old has had a smaller role on offense since Savion Williams returned from injury, but Moore still plays a key role in the kick return unit on special teams.

injuryReport.name: Bo Melton
factors: Thursday Limited Participation (LP); player toughness prior = 76%
injuryReport.beatComment: Melton had a trio of limited practices leading up to the Packers' Week 12 matchup against the Rams. The 27-year-old injured his thigh in the team's Week 10 loss to the Vikings. The fifth-year pro has appeared in all 10 games for Green Bay this season, catching five of 10 targets for 34 yards.

injuryReport.name: Kevin Zeitler
factors: Thursday Limited Participation (LP); player toughness prior = 81%
injuryReport.beatComment: Zeitler missed Green Bay's last game before the team's Week 11 bye due to ankle and triceps injuries, and it looks like his availability for Week 12 is truly up in the air. If he can't go Wednesday, the Packers could end up being perilously thin on the interior of their offensive line, as starter Sean Rhyan (ankle) and key backup Travis Glover (shoulder) are also questionable.

injuryReport.name: Sean Rhyan
factors: Thursday Limited Participation (LP); player toughness prior = 81%
injuryReport.beatComment: Rhyan sat out Green Bay's last three games before the team's Week 11 bye after suffering a high ankle sprain back in Week 7 at Detroit, and now his availability for Week 12 looks like a coin-flip proposition. If he can't suit up Wednesday, 2025 seventh-rounder John Williams may need to make another start at center against the Rams.

injuryReport.name: Travis Glover
factors: Thursday Limited Participation (LP); player toughness prior = 81%
injuryReport.beatComment: Glover appeared on Green Bay's injury report Monday with a shoulder issue, and it seems like he's truly questionable for Week 12. With starters Sean Rhyan (ankle) and Kevin Zeitler (triceps) also questionable, the Packers might be playing with a makeshift offensive line against a stout Rams defense Wednesday, though if Zeitler is able to go, Glover could shift to a backup role.

injuryReport.name: Brandon Cisse
injuryReport.beatComment: The Packers' rookie cornerback is ready to go for Wednesday's game against the Rams after he exited Week 10 early against the Vikings. Cisse has started all 10 games this season, recording 38 tackles (26 solo), including 1.5 sacks, and nine pass breakups, including an interception, on 83 percent of the defensive snaps.

coachingMatchup.headline: Sean McVay & DC Chris Shula vs. HC Matt LaFleur, OC Adam Stenavich & DC Jonathan Gannon (SoFi Stadium)
coachingMatchup.summary: Week 12 two-sided coordinator chess match pitting Los Angeles Rams's staff (Sean McVay, OC Nathan Scheelhaase, DC Chris Shula) against Green Bay Packers (6-4)—testing both Los Angeles's offensive efficiency and its defensive pass-rush and coverage discipline.
bullets: Pass-Game Efficiency & Coverage Shell Delta: Sean McVay and OC Nathan Scheelhaase pair condensed splits with pre-snap jet motion and orbit motion to stress Green Bay Packers's single-high vs. two-high rotations—widening curl/flat defenders to attack the honey-hole between hook/curl linebackers and deep safeties on play-action choice/dagger concepts.

Trench Run-Fit & Two-Way Leverage: Against Green Bay Packers's pin-and-pull, counter, and duo runs targeting the A- and B-gaps, DC Chris Shula balances four-man pressure with disguised Quarters and Cover 6 split-safety rotations on early downs and in the red zone.

Money-Down & Red-Zone Execution: Third-down conversion discipline and red-zone touchdown rate govern whether Los Angeles sustains multi-play scoring drives or yields momentum to Green Bay Packers's pass rush and coverage disguises.
Tempo, Turnovers & Venue Leverage: SoFi Stadium situational play-calling, penalty margin, and turnover differential provide the clearest late-game swing factors for both coaching staffs.

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Matthew Stafford, Colby Parkinson & Konata Mumpfield vs. CB Keisean Nixon & LB Isaiah McDuffie
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: LAR: #8 Pass Off (252.4 yds) · #8 Off. Scoring (+5.31) | GB: #10 Pass Def (-0.80)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Matthew Stafford, Colby Parkinson & Konata Mumpfield attack the intermediate seams and middle-of-the-field leverage windows against Green Bay Packers's #10 pass defense (-0.80). Winning early-down timing throws keeps Los Angeles's offense ahead of the chains and punishes disguised single-high rotations.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch Matthew Stafford (#9) scanning Packers's deep safeties at the snap—when LB Isaiah McDuffie widens to take away the crossers, the intermediate seam opens immediately for Colby Parkinson (#84).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Aaron Donald, Braden Fiske & Myles Garrett vs. QB Jordan Love & G Jordan Morgan
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: LAR: #16 Def Sacks (2.3/gm) | GB: #16 Pass Protection (6.5%)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Aaron Donald, Braden Fiske & Myles Garrett lead Los Angeles's #16 NFL pass rush (2.3/gm) against Green Bay Packers's #16 pass-protection unit (6.5%). Collapsing the interior pocket without sending extra blitzers lets Rams keep seven defenders in coverage.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: On 3rd-and-6+, watch whether Aaron Donald (#99) draw chip help from Packers's tight ends or backs—creating 1-on-1 rush lanes inside for Braden Fiske (#55).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Quentin Lake, Trent McDuffie & Kam Curl vs. WR Christian Watson & QB Jordan Love
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: LAR: #2 Pass Def (-3.73) | GB: #3 Pass Off (268.1 yds)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Quentin Lake, Trent McDuffie & Kam Curl anchor Los Angeles's #2 pass defense (-3.73) against WR Christian Watson and Green Bay Packers's #3 passing attack (268.1 yds). Limiting explosive 20+ yard chunk plays forces Packers into sustained red-zone drives.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Track Quentin Lake (#37) at the top of routes against WR Christian Watson: press-bail alignment with safety help over the top takes away QB Jordan Love's preferred isolation shots.

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Kyren Williams & Tutu Atwell vs. Packers Front Seven & LB Isaiah McDuffie
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: LAR: #7 Rush Off (133.0 yds) | GB: #14 Rush Def (-0.83)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Kyren Williams & Tutu Atwell test Green Bay Packers's #14 run defense (-0.83) with horizontal stretch and interior cutback lanes. Generating 4.5+ yards on first down unlocks play-action explosives and neutralizes Packers's pass-rush packages.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch whether Packers's linebackers over-pursue motion to the perimeter—opening decisive backside B-gap cutback lanes for Kyren Williams (#23).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Warren McClendon Jr., Kevin Dotson & Alaric Jackson vs. DT Karl Brooks & Packers Simulated Pressures
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: LAR: #16 Pass Protection (6.0%) | GB: #16 Def Sacks (2.4/gm)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Warren McClendon Jr., Kevin Dotson & Alaric Jackson protect Matthew Stafford (#16 protection at 6.0%) against DT Karl Brooks and Green Bay Packers's #16 pass rush (2.4/gm). Passing off interior twists and simulated blitzes cleanly determines late-down conversion efficiency.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch Warren McClendon Jr. (#71) on obvious passing downs—if DT Karl Brooks cannot win clean around the arc, Packers must dial up interior stunts that stress Kevin Dotson (#69).
